papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Autoencoders for End-to-End Radio Communication
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a hybrid autoencoder with a classical transmitter encoder and a quantum receiver decoder for radio communication.

assertions.value: The authors report that double data re-uploading gives another 15% improvement in the simulated autoencoder, and that the shallowest network reaching accuracy similar to the classical solution has L = 16 layers.
quotes: Introducing the double data re-uploading layer (2×DR with ansatz of Fig. 4c) leads to another 15% improvement.
the shallowest network reaching accuracy similar to the classical solution contains L = 16 layers.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from simulation in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The results are simulated, not run on a quantum device.

assertions.value: The authors state that they study simulated architectures, with a classical encoder in the transmitter and a quantum decoder in the receiver, for a single channel use (n = 1).
quotes: we study the performance of simulated architectures for standard encoded radio signals over a noisy channel.
In this work, we focus on the case of single channel use (n = 1)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract and Section II.

assertions.value: The authors state that with 1000 shots the inference time is of the order of 100ms, which is higher than the accepted level in real-time radio systems.
quotes: When the quantum decoder is executed with 1000 shots (a level already acceptable in current systems for this problem size), the inference time is the order of magnitude of 100ms which is higher than the accepted level in real-time radio systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: A calculated estimate from transpiled circuits, from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper says fewer shots could bring the time under 10ms, which it expects but does not show.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum-classical tradeoffs and multi-controlled quantum gate decompositions in variational algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusions (pages 1-2 and 11-13); skimmed section structure only for the rest.
papers.what_it_is: A study of three QAOA variants and of multi-controlled gate decompositions across native gate sets, applied to Maximum Independent Set.

assertions.value: The authors state that they find the MA-QAOA, which parameterizes each individual partial mixer, outperforms the SA-QAOA while requiring much shorter quantum circuits.
quotes: We find that the MA-QAOA, which parameterizes each individual partial mixer, outperforms the SA-QAOA while requiring much shorter quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from numerical study of MIS instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that their asymptotic gate counts show all of the compared decompositions have the same O(n) scaling, and that numerical calculations show the constant factors matter as graph size grows.
quotes: While our asymptotic gate counts show that all of the decompositions have the same O(n) scaling, our numerical calculations reveal the practical impact of the constant scaling factors as the size of the problem graph grows.
assertions.certainty_reason: The asymptotic part is analytic, but I did not read the derivations; the numerical part is empirical.

assertions.value: The authors state that they focus solely on the constraint-aware ansatz, which requires multi-controlled gates, and that the practical utility of heuristic approaches such as the QAOA remains an open question.
quotes: In this paper we focus solely on the latter case which uses the constraint-aware ansatz and therefore requires the use of multi-controlled gates.
While the practical utility of heuristic approaches such as the QAOA remains an open question
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Section 1 and its limit in Section 5.

papers.title_in_file: EVALUATING ANGLE AND AMPLITUDE ENCODING STRATEGIES FOR VARIATIONAL QUANTUM MACHINE LEARNING: THEIR IMPACT ON MODEL'S ACCURACY
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Results opening, Proposed methodology, Conclusions; tables only skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: An empirical comparison of angle and amplitude encodings in variational quantum classifiers on the Wine and Diabetes datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that, under identical model topologies, the accuracy difference between the best and worst models ranges from 10% to 30%, with differences reaching up to 41%.
quotes: The study demonstrates that, under identical model topologies, the difference in accuracy between the best and worst models ranges from 10% to 30%, with differences reaching up to 41%.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from two small datasets in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they kept the number of qubits constant and applied PCA to reduce the number of features, and that this choice disadvantaged the performance of the overall models.
quotes: the number of qubits made available to the models has been kept constant, and PCA has been applied to the considered datasets to reduce the number of features to be processed.
This choice has intrinsically disadvantaged the performance of the overall models but guarantees fairness in comparisons.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup and its limiting effect in Section 6, p.19.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Wine dataset amplitude encoding models obtained better accuracy on average, while the highest-performing model used angle encoding with an RY gate, with 10 Strongly Entangling layers and no reuploading.
quotes: models using Amplitude encoding methods have, on average, obtained better accuracy compared to those using Angle encoding
the highest-performing model in this task employed Angle encoding with an RY gate for embedding, with 10 Strongly Entangling layers and no reuploading.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result on one small dataset.

papers.title_in_file: Qubit-efficient Variational Quantum Algorithms for Image Segmentation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Results with Table I and II, Discussion and Conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A study of qubit-efficient variational algorithms (PGE, ABE and a new ACE) that cast image segmentation as a graph cut, benchmarked on synthetic images.

assertions.value: The authors report that ACE shows consistently faster convergence in training the parameterized quantum circuits than PGE and ABE.
quotes: ACE shows consistently faster convergence in training the parameterized quantum circuits in comparison to PGE and ABE.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result on synthetic images in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that Table I shows ACE can solve a combinatorial optimization problem of n variables by optimizing only log2(n) + 1 parameters, and that ACE reaches optimal solutions provided a robust classical optimizer is used.
quotes: The results in Table I reveal that ACE can solve a combinatorial optimization problem consisting of n variables by optimizing only log2(n) + 1 parameters.
Experimentally, ACE has proven to achieve optimal solutions with increased layers and parameters, provided that a robust classical optimizer is used.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result with a differential evolution optimizer, tiny images.
assertions.reader_inference: Table I covers image sizes of only a few pixels, so the log scaling claim rests on small instances.

assertions.value: The authors state that for ABE and ACE the number of circuit measurements scales exponentially with the number of qubits.
quotes: However, the number of circuit measurements scales exponentially with the number of qubits allowing us to measure the ancilla qubit state for all possible register basis states to obtain a complete binary vector solution.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit in Section VI.

assertions.value: The authors state that they benchmark PGE, ABE and ACE on synthetically generated images, focusing on quality and trainability.
quotes: We benchmark PGE, ABE and ACE on synthetically generated images, focusing on quality and trainability.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the abstract.

papers.title_in_file: Experimental quantum natural gradient optimization in photonics
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Experimental results, Conclusion; supplement not available in the file.
papers.what_it_is: An experiment that runs a variational quantum eigensolver with quantum natural gradient on a programmable photonic chip for the He-H+ cation.

assertions.value: The authors report that after correcting a constant systematic shift, all absolute errors in the He-H+ dissociation curve are less than 3.938 KJ mol−1 (0.0015 Hartree), achieving chemical accuracy.
quotes: all absolute errors are less than 3.938 KJ mol−1 (0.0015 Hartree), achieving chemical accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: An experimental result from one device and one molecule.
assertions.reader_inference: The result holds only after a constant-shift correction, which the authors cite from earlier work.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QNG-based VQE shows superior convergence speed over vanilla gradient descent, achieving more than half of the reduction in optimization iterations.
quotes: The QNG-based VQE shows superior convergence speed over vanilla gradient descent, achieving more than half of the reduction in optimization iterations.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The Conclusion words the same result as almost half of the reduction, so the paper states it two ways.

assertions.value: The authors state that they used a fully programmable photonic chip to estimate the QNG in photonics for the first time, and that they compare vanilla-gradient VQE and QNG-based VQE on the ground state of the He-H+ cation.
quotes: We utilized a fully programmable photonic chip to experimentally estimate the QNG in photonics for the first time.
We compare the convergence performance of vanilla-gradient-based VQE and QNG-based VQE in finding the ground state of the He-H+ cation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the abstract and Introduction.

papers.what_it_is: A proposal and simulation of a quantum probabilistic perceptron trained with a quantum log-likelihood on density matrices.

assertions.value: The authors report that for toy data sets the quantum perceptron is better at assigning probability to noisy samples, which resulted in improved performance over a classical perceptron.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Section V, p.1 and 6
quotes: We show that this allows us to better capture noisyness in data compared to a classical perceptron.
For toy data sets we observed that the quantum perceptron is better at assigning probability to noisy samples, which resulted in improved performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result on toy data from simulation in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the increase in performance is limited to edge cases where there is discrete input data with a small number of features.
quotes: This limits the increase in performance to edge cases where there is discrete input data with a small number of features.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit in Section V, p.6.

assertions.value: The authors state that by considering entangled qubits they can learn nonlinear separation boundaries such as XOR, and that the XOR problem can be learned perfectly with two qubits.
quotes: By considering entangled qubits we can learn nonlinear separation boundaries, such as XOR.
We show that the problem can be learned perfectly with two qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulated toy result in one study.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning For Classical Data
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Chapter 1 summary of contributions, Chapter 6 conclusions; the derivations in Chapters 3 to 5 not read.
papers.what_it_is: A PhD dissertation on quantum algorithms for supervised machine learning on classical data, covering learning-theory bounds, Hamiltonian simulation and dequantization, and quantum Boltzmann machines.

assertions.value: The author states that, taking into account optimal learning rates and the generalisation ability, supervised quantum machine learning algorithms fail to achieve exponential speedups.
quotes: Taking into account optimal learning rates and the generalisation ability, we show that supervised quantum machine learning algorithms fail to achieve exponential speedups.
We show that any quantum machine learning algorithm will exhibit a polynomial scaling in the number of training samples – immediately excluding any exponential speedup.
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis derives these bounds in Chapter 3; I read the summary and conclusion, not the proofs, so I do not suggest HIGH.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is conditional on the learning-theory assumptions the thesis names.

assertions.value: The author states that many of the algorithms investigated are of a theoretical nature, and that the ultimate performance test for any algorithm is a benchmark.
quotes: As many of the algorithms we investigate in this thesis are of a theoretical nature, we want to mention that the ultimate performance test for any algorithm is a benchmark
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis states this limit in Section 1.2, p.19.

assertions.value: The author states that the classical algorithm for Hamiltonian simulation indicates that the advantage of so-called quantum machine learning algorithms may not be as big as promised.
quotes: Secondly, and more important in context of this thesis, our result indicates that the advantage of so-called quantum machine learning algorithms may not be as big as promised.
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's own interpretation of a derived algorithm; I did not read the derivation.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum continual learning on a programmable superconducting processor
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion and outlook; Methods and Supplementary only skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: An experiment on an 18-qubit superconducting processor that trains a quantum classifier on three sequential tasks and uses elastic weight consolidation against catastrophic forgetting.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with elastic weight consolidation, the quantum classifier can incrementally learn and retain knowledge across the three distinct tasks, with an average prediction accuracy exceeding 92.3%.
quotes: we exploit the elastic weight consolidation strategy and show that the quantum classifier can incrementally learn and retain knowledge across the three distinct tasks, with an average prediction accuracy exceeding 92.3%.
assertions.certainty_reason: An experimental result from one device in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use 18 qubits to implement a variational quantum classifier with a circuit depth of 20 and 216 trainable variational parameters.
quotes: We choose 18 qubits (marked in orange in Fig. 1a) to implement a variational quantum classifier with a circuit depth of 20 and 216 trainable variational parameters (Extended Data Fig. 1).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the Results section, p.3.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work primarily focuses on classification tasks in supervised learning, and that extension to unsupervised and reinforcement learning has yet to be achieved in theory and experiment.
quotes: In addition, this work primarily focuses on classification tasks in the framework of supervised learning.
The extension of quantum continual learning to unsupervised and reinforcement learning presents more technical difficulties and has yet to be achieved in both theory and experiment.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit in Discussion and outlook.

assertions.value: The authors state that for sequential tasks involving quantum-engineered data, the quantum classifier achieves a better continual learning performance than a commonly used classical feedforward network with a comparable number of variational parameters.
quotes: we demonstrate that the quantum classifier can achieve a better continual learning performance than a commonly used classical feedforward network with a comparable number of variational parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical comparison on quantum-engineered data in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is on quantum-engineered data, which the authors chose; it does not cover classical data.
